ownership_reason: Only the gold holds the parse position and the parser: both are locals of the gold, created afresh on every call, and the gold alone runs the per-pattern loop and decides acceptance. The facade and hops 1-4 see only the string, the pattern array and the pattern range, and the gold reports a failed parse by throwing, so no hop can test the outcome and try the remaining patterns again without a try/catch block; a one-line reordering, shortening or shifting of the range still meets a prefix-parsing pattern first or loses a pattern that the test needs. The convention that every pattern is applied to the whole string from its start is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc ('The parse will try each parse pattern in turn. A parse is only deemed sucessful if it parses the whole of the input string.'); java.text.DateFormat.parse(String) and java.text.Format.parseObject(String) parse each string from the beginning with a new ParsePosition(0); CompositeFormat.reformat parses its input through Format.parseObject(String), and CompositeFormatTest.testUsage parses the whole of "01032005" with a SimpleDateFormat that way. The gold's own contract (the date of the first pattern that parses the whole of the string) is violated on the trigger input, which "yyyy'-'MM'-'dd" parses whole.
